title: dedicated-autoscaler: improve burst controls and fleet utilization reporting
author: Anita Kapoor
description: Context: Dedicated fleets sometimes exhaust short-term burst capacity under prolonged traffic spikes which leads to throttling events and increased P95 latency. We also lacked fine-grained fleet utilization telemetry for planning and autoscaler tuning. Motivation: provide explicit burst controls (token-bucket style) with configurable burst windows and hard/soft limits, and add per-fleet utilization rollups so SREs and product teams can understand sustained vs. transient load and make capacity decisions. This PR implements a conservative token-bucket burst controller, exposes new metrics, and adds reporting endpoints and dashboards. Changes (summary): - autoscaler: introduce BurstController with token-bucket algorithm, configurable parameters (burst_window_seconds, max_burst_tokens, soft_burst_threshold). Enforced at request admission path and integrated with existing capacity checks. - autoscaler config: add new schema fields and backward-compatible defaults. Helm chart updated to expose sensible defaults for Dedicated customers. - telemetry: emit redwood.dedicated.fleet.burst_tokens_used, redwood.dedicated.fleet.utilization_1m, and redwood.dedicated.fleet.utilization_5m. Metrics are tagged by fleet_id, region, and capacity_tier. - reporting: backend endpoint for aggregated utilization (GET /fleet/{id}/utilization?window=1m) used by Console dashboards. - docs: update dedicated autoscaling docs with examples and recommended tuning. - tests: unit and integration tests covering token bucket edge cases and utilization rollups. Rollout strategy: feature gated behind helm flag dedicated.autoscaler.enableBurstControls=false by default; rollout on staging, gradual canary, then GA. Related: ENG-7842 (autoscaler improvements), ENG-7920 (fleet telemetry), SUP-1123 (support case that motivated additional observability). Checklist: - [x] design doc reviewed by runtime and infra - [x] unit tests added - [x] integration tests against local dedicated stack - [x] telemetry validated on staging - [x] docs updated - [x] helm values and defaults updated Breaking changes and compatibility: default behavior is backward compatible when feature flag is false. When enabled, bursts are limited by token bucket but default limits match previous soft defaults to avoid surprise throttling. Performance: microbenchmark shows <=1% extra p99 latency in admission path for typical requests.
